blocks.text: 115 מוּסַף לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 115
uncertainties: The page number 115 is printed in both outer corners.
In the band crop the header's vowels are partly cut off. The pointing is read from the full-page scan.

blocks.text: הַפּוֹתֵחַ פִּתְחוֹ לְדוֹפְקֵי בִּתְשׁוּבָה: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא פְּתוּחָה יָדוֹ:
uncertainties: The word after הַפּוֹתֵחַ reads as פִּתְחוֹ, not פֶּתַח.
The dagesh in the bet of בִּתְשׁוּבָה is unclear.
וְ״מַ is the printed abbreviation for the refrain (וְכֹל מַאֲמִינִים). It is kept exactly as printed and not expanded.

blocks.text: הַצּוֹפֶה לָרָשָׁע וְחָפֵץ בְּהִצָּדְקוֹ: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא צַדִּיק וְיָשָׁר:
הַקָּצַר בְּזַעַם וּמַאֲרִיךְ אַף: וְ״מ שֶׁהוּא קָשֶׁה לִכְעוֹס:
uncertainties: Under the bet of בְּזַעַם there is an extra mark that may be a meteg or a smudge, and the vowel under the zayin could be patach or qamats.
In this line the abbreviation looks like וְ״מ with no patach visible under the mem.
לִכְעוֹס is spelled plene, as printed.

blocks.text: הָרַחוּם, וּמַקְדִּים רַחֲמִים לְרֹגֶז: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא רַךְ לִרְצוֹת:
uncertainties: On the full-page scan שֶׁהוּא looks like שֶׁחוּא (the he looks closed, like a chet). This may be a print or scan artifact. The enlarged band is ambiguous.

blocks.text: הַשָּׁוֶה, וּמַשְׁוֶה קָטוֹן וְגָדוֹל: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹפֵט צֶדֶק:
קר״ס הַתָּם וּמִתַּמֵּם עִם תְּמִימִים: וְ״מַ שֶׁהוּא תָּמִים פָּעֳלוֹ:
uncertainties: There is a small abbreviation in the right margin before הַתָּם that reads as קר״ס. Its letters are uncertain; it may be a role or responsive cue, and the first letter could be a samekh.
The vowel under the ayin in פָּעֳלוֹ is read as chataf-qamats.

blocks.text: סוגרים הארון.
uncertainties: This is a small unpointed rubric. Read literally, the glyphs look like קונריס הארון. The reading סוגרים ('close the Ark') is an interpretation of the small type and is uncertain.

blocks.text: אין פֿראַנקפֿורט אַם מאַין, אונד פֿיעלען געמיינדען ווירד תִּשְׂגַּב ניכט געבעטעט.
uncertainties: This is German in Hebrew letters, set in a Vaybertaytsh-style face where alef looks like chet. I read those glyphs as alef.
The rafe strokes on the pe letters and the vowel marks on the alefs are hard to see and are given approximately.

blocks.text: ח״ תִּשְׂגַּב לְבַדֶּךָ וְתִמְלֹךְ עַל כֹּל בְּיִחוּד: כַּכָּתוּב עַל יַד נְבִיאֶךָ
uncertainties: There is a small mark before תִּשְׂגַּב, possibly a role abbreviation such as ח״ (for the cantor). Its identity is uncertain.
The pointing of לְבַדֶּךָ and כֹּל is faint in the scan.

blocks.text: וְהָיָה יְיָ לְמֶלֶךְ עַל כָּל הָאָרֶץ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִהְיֶה יְיָ אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד:

וּבְכֵן תֵּן פַּחְדְּךָ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ עַל כָּל־מַעֲשֶׂיךָ וְאֵימָתְךָ עַל כָּל־מַה־שֶּׁבָּרָאתָ וְיִירָאוּךָ כָּל־הַמַּעֲשִׂים וְיִשְׁתַּחֲווּ לְפָנֶיךָ כָּל־הַבְּרוּאִים וְיֵעָשׂוּ כֻלָּם אֲגֻדָּה אַחַת לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ בְּלֵבָב שָׁלֵם כְּמוֹ שֶׁיָּדַעְנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ שֶׁהַשִּׁלְטָן לְפָנֶיךָ עֹז בְּיָדְךָ וּגְבוּרָה בִּימִינֶךָ וְשִׁמְךָ נוֹרָא עַל כָּל־מַה־שֶּׁבָּרָאתָ:
uncertainties: The first עַל (after אֱלֹהֵינוּ) seems to have no patach.
It is unclear whether the kaf in כֻלָּם has a dagesh.
עֹז might be read as עוֹ because of the print.

blocks.text: וּבְכֵן תֵּן כָּבוֹד יְיָ לְעַמֶּךָ תְּהִלָּה לִירֵאֶיךָ וְתִקְוָה לְדוֹרְשֶׁיךָ וּפִתְחוֹן פֶּה לַמְיַחֲלִים לָךְ שִׂמְחָה לְאַרְצֶךָ וְשָׂשׂוֹן לְעִירֶךָ וּצְמִיחַת קֶרֶן לְדָוִד עַבְדֶּךָ וַעֲרִיכַת נֵר לְבֶן־יִשַׁי מְשִׁיחֶךָ בִּמְהֵרָה בְּיָמֵינוּ:
uncertainties: It is unclear whether the bet in בְּיָמֵינוּ has a dagesh.

blocks.text: וּבְכֵן צַדִּיקִים יִרְאוּ וְיִשְׂמָחוּ וִישָׁרִים יַעֲלֹזוּ וַחֲסִידִים בְּרִנָּה יָגִילוּ וְעוֹלָתָה תִּקְפָּץ־פִּיהָ. וְכָל־הָרִשְׁעָה כֻּלָּהּ כְּעָשָׁן תִּכְלֶה כִּי תַעֲבִיר מֶמְשֶׁלֶת זָדוֹן מִן־הָאָרֶץ:
uncertainties: The mappiq in כֻּלָּהּ looks present but faint.

blocks.text: אין פֿירט אונד אייניגען אַנדערען געמיינדען שטימט היער דער פֿאָרבעטער נאָך וְיֶאֱתָיוּ אַן. אין פֿראַנקפֿורט אַם מאַין, מעץ אונד דען מייזטען געמיינדען ווירד עס אָבער ניכט געזאַגט.
uncertainties: This is German in Hebrew letters, Vaybertaytsh-style; the glyphs that look like chet are read as alef.
שטימט is uncertain; it may look like סמַטעט.
The pointing of the cue word ויאתיו in the rubric is unclear.
The rubric is printed over three lines, with the last line centered.

blocks.text: וְיֶאֱתָיוּ כֹּל לְעָבְדֶךָ. וִיבָרְכוּ שֵׁם כְּבוֹדֶךָ. וְיַגִּידוּ בָאִיִּים צִדְקֶךָ. וְיִדְרְשׁוּךָ עַמִּים לֹא יְדָעוּךָ. וִיהַלְלוּךָ כָּל־אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ. וְיוֹמְרוּ תָמִיד יִגְדַּל יְיָ. (וְיִזְבְּחוּ
uncertainties: The page ends mid-hymn, and the text continues on the next page. The opening parenthesis before וְיִזְבְּחוּ is printed.
וְיוֹמְרוּ is spelled exactly as printed (vav-yod-vav-mem-resh-vav), not normalized to וְיֹאמְרוּ.
כֹּל may be printed without vowels.
It is unclear whether the bet in בָאִיִּים has a dagesh.

blocks.text: 115 Musaph for the New Year 115
uncertainties: The page number is printed in both corners in old-style numerals.

blocks.text:
He opens the gates for those who knock in repentance.
    All believe that His hand is open.
He waits for the evil-doer and delights in his justification.
    All believe that He is righteous and upright.
He shortens anger and holds back wrath.
    All believe that He is hard to anger.
Compassionate, He lets mercy precede wrath.
    All believe that He is soft to appease.
He is just and treats small and great equally.
    All believe that He is a righteous judge.
He is perfect and shows perfection with the flawless.
    All believe that His work is flawless.
uncertainties: In 'evil-doer and', the 'a' of 'and' is malformed and looks like '3and'. It is read as 'and'.
A stray macron-like mark above 'He' in 'He is just' is a print or scan artifact and is left out.

blocks.text: In Frankfurt a. M. and many congregations תשגב is not said.
uncertainties: תשגב here is an embedded Hebrew cue word, not translation.

blocks.text: תשגב
Thou alone wilt be exalted and reign alone over all. As it is written through Thy prophet: The Lord will be King over the whole earth, on that day will the Lord be One and His Name One.
uncertainties: Printed in smaller type than the surrounding paragraphs.
The quoted verse is Zechariah 14:9. It is not marked off separately in the English.

blocks.text: ובכן

And therefore put the fear of Thee, O Lord our God, upon all Thy works and awe of Thee upon all that Thou hast created, so that all works may fear Thee and all the created bow down before Thee and all of them may be made into one group for the performance of Thy will with a complete heart, since we know, O Lord our God, that dominion lies before Thee, that strength is in Thy hand and might in Thy right hand and that Thy Name inspires with awe all that Thou has created.
uncertainties: 'Thou has created' (not 'hast') is printed this way and kept as is.

blocks.text: ובכן

And therefore grant honour, O Lord, to Thy people, fame to those who fear Thee and praise to those who seek Thee and confidence to those who wait for Thee, joy to Thy land happiness to Thy city and a rise of fortune to David Thy servant and an array of light to the son of Jesse Thine anointed speedily and in our days.
uncertainties: There is no comma between 'land' and 'happiness'; this is kept as printed.

blocks.text: ובכן

And thus may the righteous see and rejoice and the upright exult and the pious revel with joy. Vice shall close its mouth and all evil entirely disappear like smoke when Thou removest the dominion of arrogance from the earth.
In Fuerth and other communities the reader now sings: ויאתיו but in Frankfurt a. M., Metz and many communities this prayer is omitted.
uncertainties: A stray mark above 'In' is an artifact and is left out.
ויאתיו here is an embedded Hebrew cue word.

blocks.text: ויאתיו
All will come to serve Thee and praise Thy glorious Name, They will proclaim among the islands Thy righteousness: Peoples that did not know Thee will seek Thee and all the ends of the earth will
uncertainties: The page ends mid-sentence, and the text continues on the next page.
Printed in smaller type.
The capital 'They' after the comma is as printed.

notes: Scans s250 (Hebrew) and s251 (English) are facing pages, both printed page 115 of Musaf for the first day of Rosh Hashanah.

These scans contain no Kedushah and no Unetaneh Tokef. The instruction about the lower Kedushah on 238–239 does not apply here. The pages run from the end of the וְכֹל מַאֲמִינִים piyyut through תִּשְׂגַּב and the three וּבְכֵן paragraphs to the start of וְיֶאֱתָיוּ.
The וְ״מַ refrain abbreviation is kept as printed and not expanded, because the printed text uses the abbreviation itself.
The Vaybertaytsh rubrics are given in standard Hebrew letters, with alef-like glyphs read as alef. Diacritics inside these rubrics are approximate.
Linkage cues on the English page (תשגב, ובכן ×3, ויאתיו) are separate blocks and are not part of the translations.
Both pages break off mid-text: the Hebrew at '(וְיִזְבְּחוּ' and the English at '...the ends of the earth will'.
Hebrew blocks are split at printed paragraph and stanza breaks. Each piyyut line is kept as one block containing both its half-line and its refrain.
